mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate level, relative to its 12-month moving average, is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns: a rate below the 12-month average predicts positive 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises by more than 0.2% and the consumer price index (CPI) rises by more than 0.3% in the last month, it predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rise > 0.2% AND CPIAUCSL rise > 0.3% in the last month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% in the last month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime defined by unemployment rate below 4.0% and labor force growth exceeding 0.5% in the last month, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days are positive.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 AND PAYEMS growth > 0.5% in the last month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4.0 and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% in the last month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
